AssignmentRecipient.Definition: The variable, field, or location that receives the value of an assignment.

Attribute.Definition: Attributes add extra information (metadata) to code elements like classes, methods, or properties. Attributes are often used to control behavior or provide instructions to tools and frameworks.

BaseType.Definition: A base type specifies a type that another type inherits from or implements. It defines a parent relationship in the type hierarchy.

CatchExceptionType.Definition: The type of exception this {c:color-purple keyword}catch{/c} block is designed to handle. It identifies what kind of error occurred during program execution.

ConditionValue.Definition: A value or expression that evaluates to {c:bold}true{/c} or {c:bold}false{/c}.<break/>Any expression that returns a {c:color-blue keyword}bool{/c} can be used here, including comparisons, logical operations, and method calls.

EventFieldType.Definition: An event field type defines the delegate type used by an event. It determines the shape of the methods that can handle the event.

EventPropertyType.Definition: The delegate type for an event that has explicit {c:color-blue keyword}add{/c} and {c:color-blue keyword}remove{/c} accessors. It determines the signature of methods that can subscribe to the event.

ForEachLoopCollection.Definition: The collection being iterated over in a {c:color-purple keyword}foreach{/c} loop.

GenericTypeParameter.Definition: This identifier is a placeholder that will be replaced by a concrete type when the generic type or method is used.<break/>By convention, type parameters are often named {c:code}T{/c} or prefixed with {c:code}T{/c}, such as {c:code}TKey{/c} or {c:code}TValue{/c}.

LockTarget.Definition: The variable that a {c:color-blue keyword}lock{/c} statement uses to control access to the protected code block. Only one execution thread can hold the lock on this target at a time.

ParameterLabel.Definition: A parameter label names an argument when calling a method. It makes it clear which parameter a value is being assigned to.

TargetMember.Definition: The member name that identifies the property, field, method, or event being accessed on an instance or type.

TernaryCondition.Definition: The boolean value that determines whether the {c:bold}true{/c} or {c:bold}false{/c} expression is returned.

TupleElementName.Definition: A tuple element name gives a readable name to a value inside a tuple. It makes tuple values easier to understand and access.

Type.Definition: The name of a type referenced in a {c:color-blue keyword}using{/c} directive, either being imported into the current scope or assigned an alias.

WithExpressionSource.Definition: The existing value that a {c:color-blue keyword}with{/c} expression copies before applying the specified changes. It provides the starting state for the new value.

NamespaceAliasDeclaration.Definition: An alias name that represents a {c:color-blue keyword}namespace{/c}. It allows shorter or alternative naming when referencing types within that namespace.

TypeAliasDeclaration.Definition: An alias name that represents a specific type. It provides an alternate name for a type, including generic or fully qualified types.

Invocation.Definition: The name of a method, constructor, or function being called.

LocalDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a variable, constant, or local function inside a method, accessor, or block. This identifier can be referenced only within the enclosing scope in which it is defined.

MemberDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a type member (method, property, field, event, constructor, or operator). Its visibility is determined by its {c:bold}access modifier{/c}.

ParameterDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a value that needs to be passed to a method, constructor, or lambda function. This identifier can be referenced only within the body of the member or expression in which it is defined.

AliasQualifier.Definition: An alias qualifier refers to an alias used to access a type or namespace. It helps distinguish which aliased name is being used.

CollectionInstanceQualifer.Definition: The identifier of a collection being used to access one of its elements.

ImplicitInstanceQualifier.Definition: The identifier of an object instance used to qualify access to one of its members, where the instance is implied by context.

InstanceQualifier.Definition: The identifier of an object instance used to access one of its members.

NamespaceQualifier.Definition: A segment of a fully qualified {c:color-blue keyword}namespace{/c} path used to locate a type.

TypeDeclaration.Definition: The identifier for a {c:color-blue keyword}class{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}struct{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}record{/c}, {c:color-blue keyword}enum{/c}, or {c:color-blue keyword}interface{/c}. The elements defined inside this type are the type members. This identifier can be used to access the members inside.

GroupContinuationRangeVariable.Definition: A variable introduced after a {c:color-blue keyword}group...into{/c} clause in a query. It represents the grouped results and allows them to be queried further.

GroupElement.Definition: The value or expression that a {c:color-blue keyword}group{/c} clause places into each resulting group. Each item in the final group comes from this element expression.

JoinIntoRangeVariable.Definition: A variable introduced by the {c:color-blue keyword}into{/c} keyword in a join clause. It holds the grouped matches from the join.

JoinRangeVariable.Definition: A variable used during a join operation in a query. It holds values being compared between data sources.

JoinSource.Definition: The data source being joined in a query. It provides the values used for matching during the join.

LetVariable.Definition: A variable that stores the result of an expression inside a query. It helps simplify complex expressions and allows computed values to be reused.

QuerySource.Definition: The data source being queried in a LINQ expression. It is the starting point for the query.

QueryVariableReference.Definition: A reference to a variable that was introduced earlier in the same query expression.

RangeVariable.Definition: A variable that represents a single element from a data source as the query iterates over it.
